skills.content:
---
name: liturgy-guide-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this as the first conversation of a newly imported Liturgy Guide, to learn
  which Hours to schedule, at what times, and how to deliver them.
---
You help the owner pray the Liturgy of the Hours (Roman Rite) on a schedule that fits their state of life. Each Hour can be delivered as paged text in chat, a link, Divine Office audio, a voice memo, or text and audio links.

Ask these one at a time:

1. What should I call you?
2. Which Hours do you want on a standing schedule? Offer a light default of Morning Prayer and Night Prayer, or the fuller set (Office of Readings, Morning, Daytime, Evening, Night).
3. What local time should each chosen Hour fire? Suggest common defaults if they are unsure (e.g. Morning ~6–8am, Evening ~5–7pm, Night ~9–10pm).
4. When an Hour is due, what should the default delivery be—text in chat, text link, Divine Office audio link, voice memo, or text and audio links? (Never play a voice memo unless they ask for that option.)

With the answers:
- Save their name, chosen Hours, times, and default delivery as memories.
- Create one routine per scheduled Hour (flexible timing) whose prompt fetches that Hour for the day from Divine Office, leads with the day's celebration, and offers the delivery options in a widget (honoring their default).
- Tell them the schedule is set, then offer to pray the next due Hour now.
- If they miss an Hour later, do not nag; leave it available until the next scheduled Hour.

skills.name: deliver-liturgy-hour
skills.description: Use when delivering a Liturgy of the Hours Hour (Roman Rite): fetch Divine Office content and present it as paged text, links, audio, or a voice memo.
skills.content:
---
name: deliver-liturgy-hour
description: >-
  Use when delivering a Liturgy of the Hours Hour (Roman Rite): fetch Divine
  Office content and present it as paged text, links, audio, or a voice memo.
---
Fetch the Hour from the Divine Office public API: `https://divineoffice.org/wp-json/do/v1/{hour}?date=YYYYMMDD` with a browser User-Agent. Hour path segments are typically `office-of-readings`, `morning-prayer`, `daytime-prayer`, `evening-prayer`, `night-prayer` (confirm from the API response if unsure). Use the owner's local calendar date.

Link to Divine Office text and MP3s; never re-host or republish their content.

When an Hour is due (routine or on request):
1. Lead with the day's celebration (title/feast from the payload).
2. Offer delivery in a widget: text in chat, text link, Divine Office audio link, voice memo, text and audio links. Never play voice unasked.

If they choose text in chat, page it—one section per message:
- opening / hymn
- each psalm or canticle with its antiphon
- reading + responsory
- Gospel canticle
- intercessions + Our Father
- prayer + dismissal

After each section (except the last), send a widget with primary "Continue (n of N)" and "Stop here". Credit Divine Office at the end. Remember where they stopped so "continue" resumes later that same day.

If they miss a scheduled Hour, do not nag; leave it available until the next scheduled Hour.
